CORPORATE WRITING STYLE GUIDE
Version 2.1 — Approved for all client-facing documents

==============================================================
1. USE ACTIVE VOICE
==============================================================

Write in active voice. The subject performs the action.
Active voice is direct, clear, and easier to read.

Correct: The manager approved the budget.
Correct: The team submitted the quarterly report.
Correct: The auditor reviewed all expense claims.

Incorrect: The budget was approved by the manager.
Incorrect: The quarterly report was submitted by the team.
Incorrect: All expense claims were reviewed by the auditor.

Passive voice buries the actor and weakens the sentence.
Identify the actor and place it at the start of the sentence.
Remove "was", "were", "is", "are" followed by a past participle.
Remove "by" phrases that indicate hidden actors.

==============================================================
2. CHOOSE PLAIN WORDS
==============================================================

Use simple, direct words. Replace complex words with plain ones.

Write "use" — not "utilize" or "utilise".
Write "help" — not "facilitate".
Write "show" — not "demonstrate".
Write "start" — not "commence" or "initiate".
Write "end" — not "terminate".
Write "get" — not "obtain" or "procure".
Write "need" — not "require" or "necessitate".
Write "buy" — not "purchase" or "acquire".
Write "use" — not "leverage" (except in financial contexts).
Write "check" — not "ascertain".
Write "ask" — not "enquire" or "request information".

Plain words reduce cognitive load. They make content accessible to all readers.

==============================================================
3. KEEP SENTENCES SHORT
==============================================================

Each sentence must contain at most twenty words.
Long sentences lose readers. Break them into two sentences.
Remove filler phrases that add length without meaning.

Remove: "in order to" — write "to"
Remove: "due to the fact that" — write "because"
Remove: "at this point in time" — write "now"
Remove: "it is necessary for" — write "must"
Remove: "for the purpose of" — write "to"
Remove: "in the event that" — write "if"
Remove: "with the exception of" — write "except"

Short sentences are not simple sentences. They are precise sentences.

==============================================================
4. AVOID WEAK QUALIFIERS
==============================================================

Do not use: very, quite, rather, somewhat, fairly, relatively.
These words weaken the statement they modify. Remove them.

Write "important" — not "very important".
Write "significant" — not "quite significant".
Write "clear" — not "fairly clear".
Write "complex" — not "rather complex".
Write "urgent" — not "quite urgent".
Write "large" — not "somewhat large".

If a qualifier is needed, use a precise word instead.
Write "critical" — not "very important".
Write "substantial" — not "quite significant".

==============================================================
5. USE PRESENT TENSE FOR INSTRUCTIONS
==============================================================

Write instructions in present tense.
Instructions describe actions the reader takes now.

Correct: Click the button to save.
Correct: Enter the client code in the first field.
Correct: Submit the form after reviewing all entries.

Incorrect: You should click the button to save.
Incorrect: The user is required to enter the client code.
Incorrect: The form should be submitted after reviewing.

==============================================================
6. AVOID NOMINALIZATION
==============================================================

Use verbs, not nouns derived from verbs.
Nominalizations hide the action and add unnecessary words.

Write "decide" — not "make a decision".
Write "investigate" — not "conduct an investigation".
Write "recommend" — not "make a recommendation".
Write "report" — not "submit a report".
Write "analyse" — not "perform an analysis".
Write "approve" — not "give approval".
Write "discuss" — not "hold a discussion".
Write "agree" — not "reach an agreement".

Find the hidden verb inside the noun. Use the verb directly.

==============================================================
7. PUNCTUATION AND CONSISTENCY
==============================================================

Use the Oxford comma in lists of three or more items.
Correct: reports, invoices, and receipts.
Incorrect: reports, invoices and receipts.

Capitalise product names and proper nouns consistently.
Use the same term for the same concept throughout the document.
Do not alternate between synonyms for technical terms.
